outcome: A rejected submission tells the worker what refused it, so there is nothing left to bisect: the submit path names the failing field or bound back to the model in its correction, the correction loop stops treating the first schema-valid payload as the authoritative answer, and a payload whose own summary declares itself a probe can never seal as a design, an implementation, or a captain decision - closing sworn#245, whose six placeholder seals across four native-lane-honesty runs included a captain PROCEED whose entire content was the string "probe: minimal submission to isolate field validation".

exclude: the provider-side tool schema and the sworn_submit input schema string (unchanged; this slice changes what a rejection says, not what a submission may contain)
the yield path and its recoverable-input shapes (a yield is not a submission and its correction accounting is R3-S7's seam)

operator patch 8 as it stands (the content floor is the seed for A3, not the mechanism: a floor raises the price of probing and the native-lane-honesty run showed the next probe simply padded past it)
the automation and sandbox refusal boundaries (sworn#250 and sworn#251 are the same shape at different seams and are their own slices in this release)

acceptance.text: A rejection names what refused it. Every refusal path in toolSession.submit (internal/driver/tools.go, from the decodeStrict bound through closedObject, materializeExactBytesPaths, decodeToolSubmission, the planner scope-lint branch, EncodeSubmission, Permission.validate and the YIELD_FIRST_REQUIRED branch) returns, through rejectSubmission, a correction the model can act on: which field, or which bound, refused - not a bare code. The bisecting behaviour this slice exists to remove is a rational response to an unnamed refusal, so the measure of A1 is that a worker never needs a second submission to learn what was wrong with the first. Pinned by tests over each refusal branch asserting the named field or bound reaches the correction the model receives.

A probe cannot become a work product. The correction loop stops treating the first schema-valid payload as the final answer: a submission whose own summary or detail declares it a probe or a test of the submit surface is refused as a correction rather than sealed, and never becomes a sealed_driver_handoff. The models are already honest about this - every one of the six native-lane-honesty placeholder seals said so in its own summary field ("test", and "probe: minimal submission to isolate field validation" on the captain review that then sealed as a PROCEED) - so the engine reading its own record is the whole mechanism. Pinned by a test that submits each of the observed real-world probe payloads verbatim and finds a correction and no seal.

A content floor stays as defence in depth, and says so. The operator patch carried during native-lane-honesty (a floor rejecting a summary under 120 bytes or a detail under 200 bytes for planner_proposal, implementer_design, implementer_implementation, captain_review and work_verification, via the bounded-correction path, with assembly_verification exempt) lands as product with its refusal named per A1. It is explicitly the second line, not the first: the release's own evidence is that a floor alone is insufficient, because the next probe padded past it while self-declaring as "isolation test summary padded to reasonable length to avoid floor issues". Pinned by tests over the floor boundaries and by a test asserting a padded self-declared probe is still refused by A2.

Corrections stay bounded and honest. A refusal that names a field consumes one bounded correction and keeps the session alive exactly as rejectSubmission does today (internal/driver/tools.go, submitCorrections against MaxSubmissionCorrections), never consumes a dispatch try, and never converts a nameable refusal into a terminal SUBMISSION_CORRECTIONS_EXHAUSTED that a worker could not have avoided. Every correction is durably accounted on the existing recovery-step surface so the operator can see a worker being told the same thing repeatedly. Pinned by a test asserting a named refusal costs one correction and no try, and that a worker acting on the name succeeds on its next submission.

constraints: A named refusal must not become a wider admission. Every check that refuses today still refuses after this slice; the only change is that the refusal says why. A reader must be able to confirm from the diff that no validation was relaxed to make a message easier to produce.
The name reaches the model, not only the journal. A refusal whose detail is durable but invisible to the worker leaves the bisecting incentive exactly where it was, which is the defect.

No submitted byte is trusted on the way back out: a refusal message may quote a field name or a bound, never the offending payload content, so a malformed or hostile submission cannot use the correction channel as an echo surface.

The probe guard reads the worker's own declaration, never a heuristic about quality. Refusing short or unhelpful work is A3's bounded floor; A2 refuses only a payload that says of itself that it is a probe or a test of the submit surface, so honest short work is never silently discarded as suspected probing.
